hero.headline: Draft picks power new-look St. Lucie Mets in 14-6 rout of Dunedin
hero.teaser: Four 2026 draft picks combined for nine hits and three home runs, while Clay Holmes threw four scoreless innings in a rehab appearance.
hero.body:
Four members of the New York Mets’ 2026 draft class made immediate impacts Tuesday night as the St. Lucie Mets overwhelmed the Dunedin Blue Jays 14-6 at TD Ballpark.

Aiden Robbins, Ryan Tayman, John Smith III and Kooper Schulte combined to go 9-for-17 with three home runs, two doubles, seven RBIs and seven runs scored in their professional debuts. The St. Lucie lineup also featured Yovanny Rodriguez and Wyatt Vincent, who made their team debuts after being promoted from the Florida Complex League.

The revamped offense provided more than enough support for New York Mets pitcher Clay Holmes, who moved his rehabilitation assignment from Triple-A Syracuse to the Florida State League because of predicted bad weather in New York.

Holmes, recovering from a right fibula injury, scattered two singles and two walks over four scoreless innings. He struck out three and threw 59 pitches.

Tayman gave St. Lucie a 2-0 lead in the second inning by hitting a two-run home run on the first swing of his professional career. The ninth-round selection out of Cal Poly finished 4-for-5 with a homer, a double, two singles, three runs scored and two RBIs.

Robbins, a third-round pick from Texas, drove an RBI double off the center-field wall in the third inning for his first professional hit.

The Mets added three runs in the fourth. Cole Mathis delivered a sacrifice fly before Marco Vargas lined a two-run double off the left-field wall against Dunedin starter Blake Purnell, extending the lead to 6-0.

Smith, a 19th-round pick from UCF, hit a two-run homer off Purnell in the fifth inning for his first professional hit. He homered again in the ninth and finished 2-for-5 with three RBIs.

Austin Warren, beginning a rehabilitation assignment for a right forearm strain, pitched a scoreless fifth inning with one strikeout and induced a double play. He was credited with the win.

Dunedin scored four runs against Tyler McLoughlin in the sixth, but Ernesto Mercedes stopped the rally with consecutive strikeouts. Mercedes then retired the Blue Jays in order in the seventh and added two more strikeouts.

Elian Peña hit a two-run homer in the eighth, and Robbins added an RBI single to push St. Lucie’s lead to 11-4.

The Mets scored three more runs in the ninth on Smith’s second homer, a bases-loaded walk by Julio Zayas and an RBI single from Vargas. Vargas finished 3-for-5 with three RBIs.

Schulte, a 20th-round pick from Iowa, went 1-for-3 with a single, a walk, a hit-by-pitch and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs in his St. Lucie debut, while Vincent went 1-for-4 with a double, a walk and a run.

The Mets improved to 12-18 in the second half and 45-51 overall. Dunedin fell to 14-16 in the second half and 44-51 overall.

The teams continue the series Wednesday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Martin County Fire Rescue could lose 116 firefighters, close stations if property tax reform passes
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli warned commissioners Tuesday that a proposed property tax reform on the November ballot could force sweeping cuts to fire and rescue operations. The reform would expand homestead exemptions, potentially reducing the department's budget and forcing the closure of fire stations, ending hazmat, dive, and technical rescue programs, grounding the department's critical care helicopter, and using firefighting tools past their operational lifetime. The department could be forced to cut as many as 116 firefighters over the next two years.

Cianciulli told commissioners the cuts would affect response capabilities. If incidents go beyond the tools or skill sets available on scene, the department would need to call outside agencies. Residents who attended the commission meeting had mixed reactions. One resident said the fire service was valuable above other concerns, while another questioned why cutting personnel pay was not considered among the options.

Commissioners expressed differing views on how to respond if the reform passes. Commissioner Edward Ciampi said the county would need to do belt tightening and slash budgets elsewhere. Commissioner Eileen Vargas said the county only has so many dollars to go around and needs to tighten up.

No decisions were made Tuesday. The presentation was an opportunity to gather information so the county can plan ahead of the November vote. County documents show Martin County Fire Rescue projects it could lose about one third of its workforce because of reduced property tax revenue tied to the proposed amendment. County leaders previously said about 93 percent of the Fire Rescue budget is dedicated to personnel, leaving few options to absorb the projected revenue loss.

cards.headline: Martin County warned of longer emergency response times, higher insurance premiums under tax amendment
cards.teaser: Martin County Commissioner James Blake Capps said the proposed homestead exemption expansion could lead to serious consequences including station closures and higher homeowner insurance premiums for residents.
cards.body:
Commissioner Capps said Martin County has been used to the very best in fire rescue services and he would hate to see the level of service suffer greatly if the constitutional amendment passes. Previous county projections have outlined possible station closures, reductions to specialized teams including HAZMAT, Technical Rescue, the dive team and LifeStar, and delays in replacing equipment. Officials warned the proposed cuts could lead to longer emergency response times and affect specialized emergency services provided throughout Martin County.

Capps said another serious consequence for Martin County residents would be higher insurance premiums. Residents within five miles of a fire station receive a break on homeowner's insurance, but those farther than five miles pay higher premiums. If the county shuts down three fire stations, many people would end up paying more for homeowner's insurance. Response times for people living near closed stations would increase, which could have very serious consequences for residents.

Fire Rescue leaders are expected to discuss potential operational changes if revenue reductions occur. County leaders said there would need to be a no-overtime policy for all fire rescue personnel, which would mean no backfilling of stations with personnel and would result in randomized brownouts of stations. Voters will have the final say on the constitutional amendment during the November general election.

cards.headline: New $70 million K-8 school breaks ground in Fort Pierce, will consolidate three St. Lucie County schools
cards.body:
A groundbreaking ceremony marked the start of construction on a new K-8 school in Fort Pierce that will combine three St. Lucie County schools into one state-of-the-art facility. The new school will be built on land behind Dan McCarty Middle School and is expected to welcome between 1,500 and 1,800 students when it opens. It will consolidate Dan McCarty Middle, St. Lucie Elementary and Lawnwood Elementary into a single campus.

Superintendent Jon Prince said the project is moving forward on time, on budget, and on schedule. The new facility will feature state-of-the-art technology and serve the north part of St. Lucie County. The decision to consolidate comes as the existing schools show their age. All three were built in the 1950s and 1960s. Dan McCarty Middle Principal Latricia Stubbs-James said some of the things in the current building are antiquated.

The district is funding the $70 million project in part by selling the properties where the three older schools currently stand, offsetting the cost of maintaining aging buildings. Prince said the K-8 model is already proven across the district, which operates 11 other K-8 schools. Attendance is better, test scores are better and grades are better in the K-8s, Prince said. Stubbs-James said the K-8 model offers unique benefits for younger students, allowing kindergarten students to see what it looks like to be an eighth grader.

The new Fort Pierce K-8 school is expected to be completed in August 2028.

cards.headline: Indian River County firefighter and paramedic died by suicide in Sebastian home
cards.teaser: Indian River County Fire Rescue firefighter and paramedic Geoffrey S.
cards.body:
Indian River County Fire Rescue firefighter and paramedic Geoffrey S. Lang, 35, died by suicide at his Sebastian home on Saturday, July 25, according to a Sebastian Police Department report released this week. Sebastian police officers responded to Lang's residence at 4:18 p.m. after dispatch received a call from his wife stating that her husband shot himself in front of her.

When officers arrived, they found Lang's wife and a neighbor outside the residence. Officers and a K-9 dog entered the home and discovered Lang's body in a bedroom with an apparent gunshot wound to the head. A neighbor told officers they heard a woman yelling and screaming and then heard a single gunshot between 4 p.m. and the time officers arrived. The neighbor initially thought the sound was fireworks but recognized it as a distinctive gunshot.

An individual with Indian River County Fire Rescue pronounced Lang dead at the scene. Lowther Funeral Home transported his body to the medical examiner's office. The report notes that when one of the neighbors went to speak with Lang's wife after police arrived, the wife appeared hostile.

A funeral service for Lang will be held on Tuesday, August 5 at Community Church located at 1901 23rd Street in Vero Beach, according to Thomas S. Lowther Funeral Home Crematory. The Suicide Crisis Lifeline is available by calling or texting 988. The 211 Helpline of Palm Beach and Treasure Coast can be reached by dialing 211 or texting a ZIP code to 898211.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce residents oppose proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe that could relocate history museum
cards.teaser: Residents and history advocates are raising concerns over a proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe in Fort Pierce that could displace the St. Lucie County Regional History Museum.
cards.body:
The Port of Fort Pierce master plan draft for 2026 calls for replacing the existing area at Museum Pointe with large floating docks designed for mega yachts, along with a clubhouse, an event center and a water taxi connecting to Harbour Pointe to the north. The plan also proposes relocating the history museum. Terry Howard, a passionate advocate for St. Lucie County history, said the museum is a gem for the area and the center for the county's culture. He expressed disbelief that the county wants to put mega yachts at the location.

St. Lucie County said in a statement that no plans have been approved and feedback from the board will dictate future changes, modifications and clarifications to the draft document. Howard has started a petition opposing the proposed marina, hoping to raise awareness and preserve the location and its natural surroundings.

The draft of the master plan is expected to go before the county commission in August. Howard said the location is a fantastic place and the county's history is capsulized in the museum.

cards.body:
The new routes will begin on August 10 and will consolidate existing routes. According to the district's director of transportation Ruth, the changes address a decline in ridership and will save the district the cost of operating three bus routes. Ruth said routes that only had two tiers may now pick up an extra tier, such as a route that previously served elementary and high school now also picking up middle school students. Drivers will get paid for what they work.

The district cited a shortage of bus drivers as part of the reason for the decision. No jobs were lost as a result of the changes. Parents can track their child's bus route in real time using the MyReaxium app. The route changes also include activity buses for after-school programs.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie men flee police at 80 mph, one found hiding on roof of occupied home
cards.teaser: Two men led Port St. Lucie police on a high-speed chase before abandoning their car and fleeing on foot Monday, with one suspect found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
cards.body:
A suspected drunk driver fled Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone before he and his passenger abandoned their car and ran. According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving on Southwest Becker Road. Instead of pulling over, the driver accelerated and weaved in and out of traffic, ignoring traffic signs and signals.

 The driver and passenger abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot. A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.

 The suspects were identified as Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46. Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie opens $28.8 million police training center
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie cut the ribbon on a 54,283-square-foot police training center on the City Hall grounds after four years of construction.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie officials cut the ribbon July 24 for a 54,283-square-foot, $28.8 million police training center on the Port St. Lucie City Hall grounds, just northwest of the police department. Mayor Shannon Martin said the project ensures officers have the space, training, and resources they need to continue serving the community at the highest level.

 The three-story facility includes a 20-lane, 9,508-square-foot indoor firearms range featuring an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system, a 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms, a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater, and a dedicated defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology. The facility also includes three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division, with 19 offices and 86 workstations.

 The facility was designed by ADG Architecture and constructed by HJ High. Officer Brittany McNally said officers previously traveled to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training, and the new facility will reduce those recurring costs while allowing more efficient training. The department has 455 employees with 360 sworn officers serving a population of more than 260,000.

hero.headline: 3 arrested in St. Lucie County after 3-month-old dies from dehydration and malnutrition in Fort Pierce home
hero.body:
Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in a Fort Pierce mobile home last August. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested Nicole Maxwell, 27, the child's mother, Robert Maxwell, 61, the child's grandfather, and Vikki Koon, 38, Robert Maxwell's girlfriend, on Tuesday. The investigation began on August 20, 2025, when deputies responded to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital after Robert Maxwell and Koon brought the 3-month-old to the emergency room, where the child was pronounced dead.

The medical examiner determined the infant died from dehydration and malnutrition. Court documents describe the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach. Detective Jennifer Diaz of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said the case is one of the worst she has encountered in 20 years of law enforcement. Koon told investigators she fed the infant only twice a day and admitted that when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with baby cereal mixed in. The child lived primarily with Robert Maxwell and Koon at a mobile home in the 800 block of Silverstream Circle in Fort Pierce while Nicole Maxwell lived at her boyfriend's home in Vero Beach.

Investigators described the mobile home as having windows boarded shut, exposed electrical wiring, and live and dead cockroaches throughout. Diaz said the house was extremely hot with a bug infestation and a lack of food. A neighbor named Suzan said she had witnessed the conditions firsthand and described the home as unlivable. She said one of the other children in the home would come to her door asking for water. Four other children who were living in the mobile home, ranging in age from 2 to 10 years old, have been placed in foster care through the Department of Children and Families.

Robert Maxwell and Vikki Koon are in the St. Lucie County Jail, each on a $1.5 million bond. Nicole Maxwell is in the Indian River County Jail on no bond. She was arrested on July 23 at a home in the 300 block of 12th Street Southwest in Vero Beach. Diaz said the Department of Children and Families had been involved with the family before. Sheriff Richard Del Toro urged the public to report any signs of child abuse or neglect, stating that one phone call can be the difference between a child receiving help and a life being saved.

cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police are searching for two men in their early 20s who forced a victim to withdraw cash at gunpoint from a Wells Fargo ATM on Sunday night.
cards.body:
A man using a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce became the victim of an armed robbery on Sunday at about 8:38 p.m. when two men forced him to pull out cash before fleeing on foot. The Fort Pierce Police Department said one of the men displayed a gun concealed in his waistband before forcing the victim to withdraw an unknown amount of cash. Officers responded to the scene, established a perimeter, and used a K-9 and drone to search for the suspects, but the suspects were not located.

Police described the suspects as two men in their early 20s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt. The Fort Pierce Police Department is asking anyone with information to contact the department.

hero.headline: Big Apple Pizza in Fort Pierce expands free book program with outdoor reading room
hero.body:
Big Apple Pizza in Fort Pierce is transforming its outdoor patio into a dedicated reading room where children can pick up free books at any time. Owner Scott Van Duzer has operated a free book program inside the restaurant for years, inviting children to take home books at no cost, but the collection has outgrown the available space.

Van Duzer said seeing children discover new books has been one of the most rewarding parts of the program. The restaurant keeps shelves stocked inside, and children who visit for pizza or simply stop by for a book are welcome to take one home. Van Duzer said the goal is to make books easy to access and help encourage a lifelong love of reading.

The decision to expand comes from Van Duzer's commitment to giving back, which he credits to his mother's example. Van Duzer said his mother taught him that if he could give back, he should give back, and the restaurant lives that commitment every day. Construction on the new reading room is underway and is expected to be completed later this fall.

Until the reading room opens, children can continue picking up free books inside Big Apple Pizza at 2311 S 35th St in Fort Pierce. Van Duzer said every child is welcome to take a book home, no questions asked.

cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council has permanently banned construction of a gas station on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive in Tradition. The council unanimously approved the restriction on July 13 as part of the 16th amendment to the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development, ending nearly three months of debate over the future of land originally planned as Phase 3 of the Heritage Oaks at Tradition residential development.

 Winding River Crosstown LLC requested permission in May to convert the parcel from residential to commercial use. While council members supported commercial development, several raised concerns that a convenience store with gas pumps would worsen traffic along Crosstown Parkway west of Interstate 95. Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo and other council members asked staff to determine whether gas stations could be eliminated as a permitted use, leading the council to table the request on May 26. Heritage Oaks residents urged the council in June to reject the land-use change, citing traffic, noise and neighborhood impacts.

 The council voted 4-0 on June 22 to approve the commercial designation after the developer agreed to permanently give up the right to build a gas station. The July 13 ordinance codified that restriction into the Tradition MPUD documents, ensuring the prohibition remains with the property regardless of future ownership. City planner Bridget Kean said service stations remain permitted elsewhere in the Tradition mixed-use area but are now prohibited on Parcel 11A. The updated plan also requires the developer to install a fence along the southern property line before mass grading and to complete an architectural wall and landscape buffering along the southeastern and southern boundaries before the first building permit is issued.

 Councilman Anthony Bonna defended the public process and the decision, saying Port St. Lucie has long lacked commercial development, placing a burden on homeowners. Councilman David Pickett said the city has consistently heard residents oppose additional housing and called the shift to commercial the best outcome for the corner. Councilwoman Stephanie Morgan, who initially questioned whether prohibiting a specific business type amounted to government interference, ultimately voted with the council. Mayor Shannon Martin confirmed the restriction would remain with the property in perpetuity before the final unanimous vote.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County breaks ground on $70 million K-8 school consolidating three Fort Pierce campuses
cards.teaser: A groundbreaking ceremony marked the start of construction on a new K-8 school in Fort Pierce that will combine three St. Lucie County schools into one facility. The new school wil
cards.body:
A groundbreaking ceremony marked the start of construction on a new K-8 school in Fort Pierce that will combine three St. Lucie County schools into one facility. The new school will be built on land behind Dan McCarty Middle School and is expected to welcome between 1,500 and 1,800 students when it opens. It will consolidate Dan McCarty Middle, St. Lucie Elementary and Lawnwood Elementary into a single campus.

 Superintendent Jon Prince said the project is moving forward on time, on budget, and on schedule. The new facility will feature state-of-the-art technology and serve the north part of St. Lucie County. The decision to consolidate comes as the existing schools show their age.

 All three were built in the 1950s and 1960s. Dan McCarty Middle Principal Latricia Stubbs-James said some of the things in the current building are antiquated.

 The district is funding the $70 million project in part by selling the properties where the three older schools currently stand, offsetting the cost of maintaining aging buildings. Prince said the K-8 model is already proven across the district, which operates 11 other K-8 schools. Attendance is better, test scores are better and grades are better in the K-8s, Prince said.

 Stubbs-James said the K-8 model offers unique benefits for younger students. Kindergarten students can see what it looks like to be an eighth grader at a new K-8, she said. The new Fort Pierce K-8 school is expected to be completed in August 2028.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce residents oppose proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe over concerns for St. Lucie County Regional History Museum
cards.teaser: Residents and history advocates in Fort Pierce are raising concerns over a proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe, fearing the development could displace the area's cultural heritage and the St. Lucie County Regional History Museum.
cards.body:
The Port of Fort Pierce master plan draft for 2026 calls for replacing the existing area at Museum Pointe with large floating docks designed for mega yachts, along with a clubhouse, an event center and a water taxi connecting to Harbour Pointe to the north. The plan also proposes relocating the history museum. Terry Howard, a passionate advocate for St. Lucie County's history, expressed disbelief over the proposed changes.

 This is a gem for the area, and I just can't believe they want to put mega yachts here, he said. The museum, it's our culture. It's the center for our culture for this county.

 In a statement, St. Lucie County said that no plans have been approved and feedback from the board will dictate future changes, modifications and clarifications to the draft document. Howard has started a petition opposing the proposed marina, hoping to raise awareness and preserve the location and its natural surroundings. This is just a really fantastic place, and our history is capsulized in this museum here, he said. The draft of the master plan is expected to go before the county commission in August.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce pizza shop transforms outdoor patio into free reading room for children
cards.teaser: Big Apple Pizza in Fort Pierce is converting its outdoor patio into a dedicated reading room where children can pick up free books any time they visit. Owner Scott Van Duzer announ
cards.body:
Big Apple Pizza in Fort Pierce is converting its outdoor patio into a dedicated reading room where children can pick up free books any time they visit. Owner Scott Van Duzer announced the expansion Wednesday as the restaurant's existing free book program outgrew its indoor space.

 Van Duzer has kept shelves of free books inside the restaurant for years, inviting children to take one home at no cost. He said seeing kids light up when they discover a new book has been one of the most rewarding parts of the program. As more children have stopped by to pick up books, the collection has continued to grow and the restaurant has run out of space inside.

 The new outdoor reading room will allow children to access books whether their families come in for pizza or simply stop by for a book. Van Duzer said the goal is to make books easy to access and help encourage a lifelong love of reading. He said the commitment to giving back comes from the example his mother set while he was growing up, adding that she told him to give back if he could.

 Construction on the new reading room is underway and is expected to be completed later this fall. Until then, children can continue picking up free books inside Big Apple Pizza at 2311 S 35th St in Fort Pierce. Van Duzer said every child is welcome to take a book home, no questions asked.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County school district cuts 19 workers as Temporary Protected Status expires
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County School District is separating 19 employees from employment today as Temporary Protected Status expires for Haitian workers.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County confirmed 19 district employees will be separated from employment as all school district employees must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Chuck Ridley, director of civic engagement for the Service Employees International Union, said the union expects hundreds of workers statewide to be affected, with nearly 20 employees in the Palm Beach County School District alone.

 Ridley said many of the workers losing TPS protections are bus drivers, custodians, paraprofessionals, food service employees and city workers. He warned that without drivers to pick up students or workers to provide public services, residents will see disruptions in schools, garbage collection and other city functions. The healthcare system could also face staffing shortages, particularly in hospitals and nursing homes that rely heavily on immigrant workers.

 The Florida Healthcare Association said Haitian caregivers are valued members of the long term care workforce, serving as certified nursing assistants, nurses, dietary aides, housekeepers and other essential team members. The association said a disruption to experienced staff could create additional challenges to long term care centers focused on supporting the needs of residents, families and care teams. According to the Lar Management Group, the Haitian community contributes an estimated $1.2 billion to Florida's economy.

hero.headline: Draft picks power new-look St. Lucie Mets in 14-6 rout of Dunedin
hero.teaser: Four 2026 draft picks combined for nine hits and three home runs, while Clay Holmes threw four scoreless innings in a rehab appearance.
hero.body:
Four members of the New York Mets’ 2026 draft class made immediate impacts Tuesday night as the St. Lucie Mets overwhelmed the Dunedin Blue Jays 14-6 at TD Ballpark.

Aiden Robbins, Ryan Tayman, John Smith III and Kooper Schulte combined to go 9-for-17 with three home runs, two doubles, seven RBIs and seven runs scored in their professional debuts. The St. Lucie lineup also featured Yovanny Rodriguez and Wyatt Vincent, who made their team debuts after being promoted from the Florida Complex League.

The revamped offense provided more than enough support for New York Mets pitcher Clay Holmes, who moved his rehabilitation assignment from Triple-A Syracuse to the Florida State League because of predicted bad weather in New York.

Holmes, recovering from a right fibula injury, scattered two singles and two walks over four scoreless innings. He struck out three and threw 59 pitches.

Tayman gave St. Lucie a 2-0 lead in the second inning by hitting a two-run home run on the first swing of his professional career. The ninth-round selection out of Cal Poly finished 4-for-5 with a homer, a double, two singles, three runs scored and two RBIs.

Robbins, a third-round pick from Texas, drove an RBI double off the center-field wall in the third inning for his first professional hit.

The Mets added three runs in the fourth. Cole Mathis delivered a sacrifice fly before Marco Vargas lined a two-run double off the left-field wall against Dunedin starter Blake Purnell, extending the lead to 6-0.

Smith, a 19th-round pick from UCF, hit a two-run homer off Purnell in the fifth inning for his first professional hit. He homered again in the ninth and finished 2-for-5 with three RBIs.

Austin Warren, beginning a rehabilitation assignment for a right forearm strain, pitched a scoreless fifth inning with one strikeout and induced a double play. He was credited with the win.

Dunedin scored four runs against Tyler McLoughlin in the sixth, but Ernesto Mercedes stopped the rally with consecutive strikeouts. Mercedes then retired the Blue Jays in order in the seventh and added two more strikeouts.

Elian Peña hit a two-run homer in the eighth, and Robbins added an RBI single to push St. Lucie’s lead to 11-4.

The Mets scored three more runs in the ninth on Smith’s second homer, a bases-loaded walk by Julio Zayas and an RBI single from Vargas. Vargas finished 3-for-5 with three RBIs.

Schulte, a 20th-round pick from Iowa, went 1-for-3 with a single, a walk, a hit-by-pitch and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs in his St. Lucie debut, while Vincent went 1-for-4 with a double, a walk and a run.

The Mets improved to 12-18 in the second half and 45-51 overall. Dunedin fell to 14-16 in the second half and 44-51 overall.

The teams continue the series Wednesday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named Florida State League Pitcher of the Week
cards.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for the week of July 20-26. Minor League Baseball announced the honor Tuesday.

Ware made two appearances last week at Clover Park against Fort Myers, one start on Tuesday and one relief outing on Sunday. The southpaw combined to pitch 7.0 scoreless innings. He scattered three hits, walked two and struck out 12. The Mets won both games with Ware getting credit for the win on Sunday.

Ware, 22, was drafted by the Mets in the 15th round out of LSU in 2025. He made his pro debut with St. Lucie in April and has been with the team all season.

This is the first FSL Pitcher or Player of the Week award for the Mets this season. Ware is the first St. Lucie player to earn a Florida State League weekly honor in 2026.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named FSL Pitcher of the Week
cards.teaser: The 22-year-old left-hander struck out 12 batters over seven scoreless innings in two appearances against Fort Myers.
cards.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for July 20-26, Minor League Baseball announced Monday.

 Ware made two appearances against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels at Clover Park, starting Tuesday and returning for a relief outing Sunday. The left-hander combined to throw seven scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two walks while striking out 12 batters.

 The Mets won both games in which Ware appeared. He earned the victory Sunday after pitching four scoreless innings, allowing one hit and one walk and recording a career-high eight strikeouts as St. Lucie rallied for an 11-8 win.

 Ware, 22, was selected by the New York Mets in the 15th round of the 2025 MLB Draft out of LSU. He made his professional debut with St. Lucie in April and has remained with the team throughout the season.

cards.headline: Mets erase 5-0 deficit to beat Mighty Mussels 11-8
cards.teaser: Jeremy Rodriguez went 4-for-4, and Conner Ware struck out a career-high eight as St. Lucie scored eight runs in the second inning.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets erased an early five-run deficit with an eight-run second inning and rallied for an 11-8 win over the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Sunday afternoon at Clover Park.

 Fort Myers won the seven-game series 4-3 and finished the season series with an 8-4 advantage.

 The Mighty Mussels scored three runs in the first inning and two more in the second to build a 5-0 lead. St. Lucie responded with eight runs in the bottom of the second and moved ahead for good.

 Randy Guzman delivered the decisive hit, lining a two-out, two-run single that turned a 5-4 deficit into a 6-5 Mets lead. Julio Zayas followed with a two-run single to extend the advantage to 8-5.

 The Mets added three runs in the third. Elian Peña hit an RBI single, Jacob Reimer drove in a run with a double and Trey Snyder added a sacrifice fly to make it 11-5.

 Conner Ware took over on the mound in the third inning and settled the game down for St. Lucie. Ware pitched four scoreless innings, allowed one hit and one walk, and struck out a career-high eight batters. He struck out the side swinging in the fourth and struck out the side looking in the sixth before earning the win.

 Fort Myers scored three runs in the seventh against Luis Sotillo, who was making his Mets debut. Sotillo recovered by retiring six of the final seven batters he faced and carried the game through the eighth inning.

 Elwis Mijares worked a perfect ninth on six pitches to record his third save.

 Jeremy Rodriguez led the Mets at the plate, going 4-for-4 with a double, an RBI and two runs scored from the No. 9 spot in the order. Zayas and Peña collected two hits apiece.

 Reimer, beginning a minor league rehabilitation assignment for a groin injury, went 1-for-3 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and two runs scored. He played all nine innings at third base.

 The Mets improved to 11-18 in the second half and 44-51 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game road series against the Dunedin Blue Jays on Tuesday. First pitch at TD Ballpark is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Fall Short in 15-14 Loss to Fort Myers
cards.teaser: Randy Guzman hit two home runs and drove in six as the St. Lucie Mets nearly erased an eight-run deficit in a 15-14 loss to Fort Myers.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets nearly erased an eight-run first-inning deficit but fell one run short in a 15-14 loss to the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Saturday night at Clover Park.

 Fort Myers scored eight runs in the opening inning and survived several St. Lucie rallies to earn its third consecutive victory.

 Mets starter Ethan Lanthier was charged with seven runs on five hits and two walks before being removed with two outs in the first inning. Harry Genth delivered a three-run double during the Mussels' early outburst.

 Mets Answer With Five-Run First Inning

 St. Lucie immediately responded with five runs against Fort Myers starter Matt Barr in the bottom of the first. Antonio Jimenez, Branny De Oleo and Simon Juan each recorded RBI hits to cut the deficit to 8-5.

 The Mighty Mussels added three runs against Franyel Diaz in the third inning. Ramiro Dominguez drove in two with a single, and Byron Chourio hit a solo home run to extend the Fort Myers lead to 11-5.

 Trey Snyder helped St. Lucie pull closer in the fourth inning with an unconventional trip around the bases. Snyder's ground-ball single was mishandled by shortstop Quetin Young, who then committed a throwing error that allowed Snyder to score and another run to cross the plate.

 The play cut the Mussels' lead to 11-7.

 Guzman Homers Twice

 Randy Guzman hit a two-run homer against Ramiro Villanueva in the fifth inning to bring the Mets within two runs.

 Villanueva later hit consecutive batters and was ejected. St. Lucie loaded the bases with one out, but reliever Adam Falinski retired Elian Pena on a popout and Snyder on a groundout to preserve the 11-9 Fort Myers advantage.

 Young answered with a three-run home run over the batter's eye in the sixth, pushing the Mussels' lead to 14-9.

 Guzman responded again in the bottom half of the inning, launching a three-run homer to make it 14-12.

 He finished the game 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, six RBIs and two runs scored.

 Ninth-Inning Rally Falls One Run Short

 Ricardo Paez opened the ninth inning with a solo home run that gave Fort Myers a 15-13 lead and provided what proved to be a crucial insurance run.

 Francisco Toledo scored on a wild pitch and throwing error with one out in the bottom of the ninth. Marco Vargas then homered to right field with two outs, pulling St. Lucie within one run at 15-14.

 Brent Francisco struck out Chase Meggers to end the game and record his third save.

 Michael Hilker Jr. earned the win after pitching 2 1/3 scoreless innings of relief for Fort Myers. Lanthier took the loss.

 Jimenez went 2-for-3 with two walks and three runs scored. Vargas, De Oleo and Juan added two hits apiece.

 The Mets fell to 10-18 in the second half and 43-51 overall. The Mighty Mussels improved to 14-14 in the second half and 51-42 overall.

 The teams will conclude their series Sunday at Clover Park. First pitch is scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

cards.headline: Zayas Homers Twice as St. Lucie Mets Cruise Past Mighty Mussels
cards.teaser:
Julio Zayas homered twice and Trey Snyder continued his hot stretch at the plate as the St. Lucie Mets defeated the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels 8-2 Tuesday night at Clover Park.

The
cards.body:
Julio Zayas homered twice and Trey Snyder continued his hot stretch at the plate as the St. Lucie Mets defeated the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels 8-2 Tuesday night at Clover Park.

The victory in the series opener was St. Lucie's fifth win in its last six games.

The Mets held a 1-0 lead through two innings before breaking the game open with four runs against Fort Myers starter Eric Hammond in the third.

Randy Guzman drew a bases-loaded walk to bring home the first run of the inning. Snyder followed with a two-run double before scoring on a throwing error after Antonio Jimenez singled, extending the Mets' lead to 5-0.

Jimenez added a sacrifice fly in the fifth inning to make it 6-0.

Zayas provided the rest of St. Lucie's offense with solo home runs in the sixth and eighth innings. He became the second Mets player this season to record a multi-homer game, joining Guzman.

Zayas finished 3-for-4 with his fifth and sixth home runs of the season.

Snyder also went 3-for-3 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and a run scored. He has collected seven hits over his last two games.

St. Lucie starter Conner Ware pitched three scoreless innings, allowing no runs while striking out four.

Emilio Obispo earned the win after allowing two runs on two hits over four innings. He walked three and struck out three.

Zack Mack pitched a scoreless eighth inning before Elwis Mijares worked the ninth and induced a 4-6-3 double play to end the game.

The Mets improved to 9-14 in the second half and 42-47 overall. The Mighty Mussels fell to 10-13 in the second half and 47-41 overall.

The teams will play the second game of the series Wednesday at Clover Park. The Mets will hold their annual Summer Camp Day, with first pitch scheduled for 11:10 a.m.

cards.headline: Messi bathed Yamal as baby in 2007 photo shoot, now they meet in World Cup final
cards.teaser: A 2007 charity calendar photo shoot paired teenage Lionel Messi with infant Lamine Yamal. Now 19 years later, they face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, took the photos after Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró near Barcelona who wanted to participate.

 Soccer destiny paired her baby boy with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

 Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed with Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation.

 The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's final. Monfort, 58, is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey. He said his heart is split and he does not know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win.

hero.headline: Recycled fishing line becomes friendship bracelets at Vero Beach Museum of Art Aug. 8
hero.body:
Discarded fishing line will be transformed into friendship bracelets when the Vero Beach Museum of Art teams up with Coastal Connections for a free Second Saturday program beginning at 10 a.m. Aug. 8. Coastal Connections will lead the hands-on activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium, where visitors can make friendship bracelets using recycled fishing line collected from local waterways. Participants can also learn about the organization's Fishing Line Recycling Program. The museum has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp.

The event includes docent-led mini-tours, studio art projects and opportunities to learn about protecting local marine life. From 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., families can take short, docent-led gallery tours through the Museum Studios family program. Visitors can then participate in Nature in Layers, an art activity for children connected to the museum's exhibitions.

Guests can also tour the museum's summer exhibitions throughout the day. James Prosek: At Work is on view in the Holmes Gallery, while Jill Nathanson: Chromatic Phrases is displayed in the Schumann and Titelman galleries. Second Saturday includes free museum admission throughout the day.

Kendra Bergman, founder and executive director of Coastal Connections, said the partnership is an example of working with the community to introduce everyone to marine conservation and environmental protection. Coastal Connections was founded in 2017 with a mission of advancing the survival of sea turtles by educating and connecting people to the environment. Additional programs may include performances, lectures, films and other arts and humanities offerings on select Saturdays.

cards.headline: Big Taste of Martin County food festival returns Oct. 6 at Stuart airport
cards.teaser: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties will host its annual food and spirits fundraiser at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart, featuring local restaurants competing for awards.
cards.body:
Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties is preparing for the return of Big Taste of Martin County, a food and spirits event scheduled for Oct. 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart. The annual fundraiser brings together local restaurants, chefs and community partners to support mentoring programs for children across the Treasure Coast. Guests can sample food, wine and beer from area businesses while participating restaurants compete for Big Taste awards and local bragging rights.

The event helps fund mentorship opportunities for children who are currently waiting to be matched with a mentor, known as a Big, according to the nonprofit. Community members can support the mission by purchasing tickets, attending the event or volunteering to become a mentor. Spritz Stuart plans to feature several menu items during the event promotion, including a Tuscan salmon dish, a smash burger and a specialty cocktail called the Fig & Flame.

Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties serves children and families throughout Palm Beach and Martin counties through one-on-one mentoring relationships designed to support academic achievement, confidence and personal growth. More information about the event and mentorship opportunities is available through Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties.

hero.headline: Florida executes two men in one day, including 80-year-old in state's first double execution in over 60 years
hero.body:
Florida on Tuesday carried out two executions in a single day for the first time in more than 60 years, including an 80-year-old man who became the second-oldest inmate known to receive a lethal injection in modern U.S. history. Dominick Anthony Occhicone was pronounced dead at 6:13 p.m. at Florida State Prison near Starke, nearly five hours after James Aren Duckett, 68, received a lethal dose in the same death chamber. The state became the first in nearly a decade to execute two people on the same day, with the last such occurrence happening in Arkansas in 2017.

Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis, who has authority under Florida law to set execution dates, decided earlier this month to carry out both executions on the same day. DeSantis has made Florida's death chamber the nation's busiest at the end of his final term, saying too many families have waited too long to see justice. Since 2025 began, Florida has carried out nearly half the state executions across the country. The state has executed 12 people in 2026, more than all other states combined, with another execution scheduled for August.

Occhicone was convicted of fatally shooting his ex-girlfriend's parents in June 1986. He apologized to the family of the victims and to his own family in his final words, saying he never meant to do what he did. He is the oldest known prisoner executed in Florida since the state began modern record-keeping a century ago. Nationwide, only Walter Moody Jr., 83, who received a lethal injection in Alabama in 2018, was older at the time of execution. Duckett was convicted of raping and drowning 11-year-old Teresa McAbee while he was working as a police officer in central Florida in 1987. He declined to make a final statement.

DeSantis, who leaves office in January, oversaw a record 19 executions last year, more in a single year than any other Florida governor since the U.S. reinstatement of the death penalty in 1976. The governor has rarely commented on the pace of executions, previously noting some on death row had committed crimes as far back as the 1980s. Florida Department of Corrections records show multiple executions on a single day were more common in the past, with the last being in 1964. The U.S. Supreme Court denied last appeals from both men Tuesday.

cards.headline: Judge rejects Lt. Gov. Collins' residency challenge, keeps Fishback on Florida Republican gubernatorial primary ballot
cards.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback demanded that Lt. Gov. Jay Collins resign after a circuit judge ruled Collins failed to prove Fishback was ineligible for Florida's Republican primary ballot.
cards.body:
Circuit Judge David Frank ruled Monday that Collins failed to present enough evidence to overcome Florida's legal presumptions favoring continued residency and access to the ballot. Collins had argued that Fishback failed to satisfy the Florida Constitution's requirement that a governor reside in the state for the seven years preceding the general election. Collins' attorneys pointed to records showing Fishback voted in Washington during the 2020 presidential election, filed D.C. resident income-tax returns and signed mortgage documents identifying a condominium there as his principal residence.

Fishback testified that he never intended to abandon Florida as his permanent home, describing the Washington property as a second residence or investment. Frank acknowledged that Fishback's filings could potentially create legal or regulatory consequences in Washington, but found they did not establish that Fishback intended to surrender his Florida domicile. The judge also cited Fishback's Florida upbringing, family connections, driver's license, vehicle registration, voting history and business ties to the state.

Collins rejected Fishback's demand that he resign and said the ruling would not change his campaign. The order leaves Fishback on the Aug. 18 Republican primary ballot. Florida law awards a party's nomination to the candidate receiving the most primary votes, even without an outright majority. A Cygnal survey conducted July 12 and 13 placed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, the Trump-endorsed frontrunner, at 43%, Fishback at 12%, Collins at 11% and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 2%.

cards.headline: Florida executes former police officer convicted of killing 11-year-old girl in 1987
cards.teaser: James Aren Duckett, 68, was pronounced dead at 1:19 p.m. Tuesday at Florida State Prison, the first of two executions carried out by the state in a single day.
cards.body:
Duckett was convicted of raping and drowning 11-year-old Teresa McAbee while he was working as a police officer in central Florida in 1987. He declined to make a final statement and showed no response several minutes into the execution when the prison warden shook him and shouted his name. Duckett became the 11th Florida inmate executed this year.

 The girl's relatives spoke of decades of suffering after the execution. Dorthy Tula, the victim's mother, said she waited nearly 40 years to have him dead before breaking down. Tracy Mcfall-Buskirk, the girl's cousin, said the man took advantage of his badge. The execution was part of the first double execution in Florida in more than six decades and the first time any state has carried out two executions in one day since Arkansas in 2017.

 Florida has now conducted 12 executions to date in 2026, more than all other states combined. Gov. Ron DeSantis, who leaves office in January, oversaw a record 19 executions last year, more in a single year than any other Florida governor since the reinstatement of the death penalty in the U.S. in 1976.
